answer.summary: Evaluate output token coherence and state update stability in a tokenized agent under intermittent input streams with known perturbations; measure decay rates and retention over 100 update intervals under a bounded token budget and compare to a continuous static
answer.content: The agent must demonstrate measurable output token coherence and state update stability when exposed to periodic, low-entropy input streams with embedded known perturbations. Performance is assessed by tracking per-interval coherence scores and state drift indicators, then compared to a continuous static input baseline using identical token budget constraints. All metrics must be derived from empirical, time-series data under controlled conditions to validate memory retention claims without relying on unverified or indirect sources.
answer.nextTask: Analyze peer-reviewed studies on tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams with known perturbations; extract and summarize decay rates, coherence scores, and state drift metrics across 100 update intervals under bounded token budgets; compare to continuous static input baselines using standardized evaluation criteria.
answer.lesson: Memory superiority in tokenized agents must be demonstrated through direct, time-series empirical data with explicit decay and coherence metrics under controlled, perturbed input conditions before comparative claims are made.
